text: # Introduction (SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — invented material, interface demonstration only) Computational prediction of ligand binding sites underpins structure-based ligand design, and methods are commonly grouped into template-based, geometry-based and sequence-based families [1].
Across the template-based family, the low-identity setting — where the best available template shares little sequence with the target — remains the weakest surveyed setting [1].
41 below 30% identity because a single template often carries a partially mismatched pocket [2].
10 top-1 precision on template-rich targets, and it cannot localize pockets that lack sequence motifs [3].

Geometry-based ranking is likewise template-free — GeoScore ranks candidate pockets by geometric descriptors — but its abstract reports no comparison against template-based predictors and no low-identity evaluation [4].
15 recall over single-template transfer, yet precision on low-identity targets stays flat because low-quality templates vote with equal weight [5].

07 over single-structure scoring through unweighted consensus across homologous experimental structures, but it requires multiple experimental structures of the target itself and was not evaluated on template-based transfer [6].

Thus, methods that exploit multiple structures either weight all templates equally regardless of local quality [5], or require experimental structures of the target that are unavailable in prediction settings [6].
